description:
Our 33-Series Artisan bicycle frames are crafted from Reynolds 853 and joined with specially selected lugs. Reynolds 853 is widely referenced as the strongest (tensile strength) air-hardening steel available for bicycle frame fabrication. Introduced in 1995, Reynolds 853 was the first commercially available air-hardening steel. These key factors, among many others, are why it was selected for our 33-Series Artisan models.

After brazing the lugs, the heat-affected zone nearest to and within the lugs is hardened through the formation of martensitic crystals as it slowly cools. Properly constructed, tight-fitting lugs, combined with air-hardening 853 steel, lead to joints that are often the strongest part of the frame.

Carefully selected tube profiles combined with strengthened joints lead to a bicycle with a smooth yet extremely durable ride.

Unlike our 22-Series bicycles, our 33-Series bike frames need to be protected from moisture and oxygen. All of our 33-Series frames are coated internally with a thin yet durable and lightweight Lanolin-based rust inhibitor. Your choice of powder-coat, Cerakote, or automotive paint, combined with lug detailing, will result in a piece of art that is functional and will last many years to come.

Our 33-Series Artisan bicycles have no model names. Each frame we craft is an involved and intimate conversation about what your new bike needs to do for you.
